label: NOTE: three separable machines in one file -- a five-armed ladder over a table, a field generator and a bit detector. The fixture is what makes the arms separable: the ladder is swept over ALL 65,536 rate signals against ALL SEVEN local indices, so an arm that swallows another arm's inputs cannot hide; the generator is run with four field widths, a non-power-of-two field count and three calls in a row so the index has to survive a call boundary; the detector is armed seven ways including an all-ones target that exercises the reg != -1 test, and fed in three bites for the same reason. Both sub-blocks are compared byte for byte after every call, so a store to an unnamed offset fails.
the ladder's first arm tests the local signal against the far end's bit rather than its own
the 9600 arm and the 12000 arm are tried in the other order, which agrees for every signal that sets only one of them
the 0x0040 arm is tried before the 0x0200 arm, which is the numerically sorted order and not the object's
the 0x0080 sub-test only consults the far end, so index 2 is chosen where the object chooses 1
the 0x0080 sub-test's two answers are transposed
the last arm falls through to the no-rate answer instead of index 0
the ladder's default is index 0 rather than the no-rate value, which agrees wherever an arm fires
the local signal is read from the FINAL table, which differs from RATE_SEQ at exactly one index
the local rate index is read from the two bytes above it
the local rate index is read out of the half-duplex block instead of the DSP block
RateToSeq answers from the FINAL table
CodeRateSeq and CodeFinalRateSeq answer from each other's table
the no-rate sentinel loses its top nibble, so CodeESeq answers CodeRateSeq's
CodeRateSeq treats the no-rate index as a real one and indexes the table with it
the no-rate test is >= rather than ==, which agrees for every value the ladder can return
why: `v32_common_rate` returns one of exactly seven values -- 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and V32_RATE_NONE, which is 6 -- so `rate != 6` and `rate < 6` partition the same domain and no input can separate them.  It is registered rather than deleted because the equality is the OBJECT's: 0x82388 is `cmp $0x6,%dx` with `je`, not a `jl`, and if the ladder ever gains an eighth answer this stops being equivalent and will be reported MIScounted.  An equivalence argument is only equivalence under the checks that exist (F651).
